pageCache.text:
A Learning Adventure with Kindness
Kindness
At the heart of all we do. We guide our children to embrace challenges, learn from experiences, and celebrate each other's achievements along the way.
Christian Environment
Where children and staff feel happy, valued, and empowered as independent, confident, and creative learners.
Learning Adventure
Designed to ignite curiosity and a lifelong love of learning. From our vibrant classrooms to our outdoor spaces, we inspire awe and wonder throughout the school day.
Check out the list of our upcoming tour dates for prospective parents.
Our Headteacher's welcome
Wonersh and Shamley Green Church of England Primary School is a nurturing, inclusive community providing an excellent education for the children in our care. The school is set in idyllic natural surroundings with six acres of grounds in the beautiful Surrey Hills. We offer children a safe and secure learning environment, with wonderful woodlands nearby to explore. We love using our woodlands to learn forest skills and to support the wider curriculum. We see learning as an exciting adventure and everyone in our community as constantly learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art & DT — Wonersh and Shamley Green
pageCache.text:
Art & DT
We aim for children to develop a love of art in a wide variety of forms. High-quality art lessons inspire children to think innovatively and creatively. We value art and design as an important part of the children’s entitlement to a broad and balanced curriculum. Art and design provides the children of WSG with opportunities to develop and extend their skills and an opportunity to express their individual interests, thoughts and ideas.
We believe that art, craft and design embody some of the highest forms of human creativity. A high-quality art and design education should engage, inspire and challenge pupils, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to experiment, invent and create their own works of art, craft anddesign.
As pupils progress, they should be able to think critically and develop a more rigorous understanding of art and design. They should also know how art and design both reflect and shape our history, and contribute to the culture, creativity and wealth of our nation.
Our art curriculum provides children with opportunities to develop their skills using a range of media and materials. Children learn the skills of drawing, painting, printing, collage, textiles, 3D work and digital art and are given the opportunity to explore and evaluate different creative ideas.
Art & Design and Technology Curriculum Overview
Art Progression of Knowledge and Skills
Design and Technology Progression of Knowledge and Skills

Curriculum
A learning adventure with kindness
Adventures are the best way to learn, this is ours.
Our curriculum is told through 'Our Curriculum Stories' which map out the learning journeys our children experience as they travel through the school. Please visit the school to read these stories. Behind these stories are detailed progression maps of the knowledge and skills that can be viewed on each subject page of the website. Every unit of work has a detailed 'unit plan' which outlines the knowledge and skills that will be taught.
You can find out more by using the links below:-
The Early Years Foundation Stage is followed in our Reception Year
We follow the Primary National Curriculum
Click for a useful Parent Guide to the Primary National Curriculum
We aim to teach children how to grow into positive, responsible citizens, who can work and co-operate with others whilst developing useful knowledge and skills so that they achieve their true potential in a changing world. We aim to deliver a broad and balanced, creative curriculum which reflects our Christian school ethos and our understanding of how children learn best; being active, curious, thinking creatively, having hands-on experiences, valuing dialogue, collaborating and co-operating with one another.
We value the way in which all children are unique, and our curriculum promotes respect for the views of each individual child, as well as for people of all cultures and religions.
We value the spiritual and moral development of each child, as well as their intellectual and physical growth. Our curriculum is underpinned by the Christian ethos of our school.
We value the importance of each person in our community and organise our curriculum so that we promote co-operation and understanding between all members of our community. We respect each child in our school and treat them with fairness and honesty. We aim to enable each member of our community to be successful, and we provide equal opportunities for all the children in our school to engender self-confidence, and healthiness in mind, body and spirit.
Children learn that they are global citizens with responsibilities; they learn about diversity, sustainable development and equity.
We value our environment, and we aim, through our curriculum and especially our forest schools learning to teach respect for the natural world, and how we should care for it for future generations, as well as our own. Thinking about the UN Sustainable Development Goals is interwoven in our cross-curricular learning. Children are taught about current affairs and topics that are really relevant to them and engage them in their learning.
As much as possible we give the children opportunities to base their learning in real hands-on experiences and give them real-life problem-solving experiences.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum Enrichment — Wonersh and Shamley Green
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Enrichment
We plan for a broad and rich curriculum which includes special events in school, visitors to the school and off-site visits
We sometimes have special weeks when we work off timetable across year groups, giving children the opportunity to learn together through a cross-curricular and creative theme. Here are some examples:
"Christianity around the World" RE Week
An environmental art and DT week called "Building for our Future"
"See me as I am" a week on inclusion exploring disabilities
A geographical week exploring countries "Around the world"
Working with an artist in residence learning how to draw and paint animals
"Investigations" with an emphasis on Science and Maths.
Exploring stories by Julia Donaldson through the Arts with a special focus on Dance and Music.
Exploring themes of sustainability in "Protect our Planet" week.
Researching the History of our School.
"Spring into Easter" with a focus on the Christian story and new growth
"Stories through the Arts"
Classes visit places linked to their topics and visitors are welcomed into school. Our international links also enrich our curriculum and we enjoy visits from friends in Nepal, Uganda and China.
Religious Education -We take part in workshops at Guildford Cathedral and Wintershall and visit our local parish churches. Children have visited the Woking Mosque, the Weybridge Synagogue, The Neasden Mandir and Guildford Cathedral. Prayer Days working with the local parishes
Music - Children take part in collaborative projects such as Young Voices at the 02, the Magna Carta Project "The Freedom Game" and "Let my People Go" at the Royal Albert Hall and Dorking Music Festival. Children have music workshops with Earthsong linked to their topics exploring Japanese drumming, African and Chinese dance and music and the Amazing Americas.
STEM - We take part in science challenges at secondary schools, the Lions Roar competition, the Primary Engineer Award, visit Surrey University, and the NFU Farmvention competition.
Sport and Outdoor Learning- Special days devoted to sport are also organised. Children are encouraged to try out a range of different sports and take part in local sporting events and competitions. We have a Surrey Outdoor Learning Adventure Day, classes visit Box Hill, Sayers Croft and Henley Fort.
School Sleepover in school
Henley Fort Outdoor Learning Centre (2 nights sleeping in yurts)
Ironbridge (3 nights in a YHA hostel)
CYE Sailing Centre in Chichester (4 nights)

French and Modern Foreign Languages
The teaching of Modern Foreign Languages, particularly French, which begins in Year 1 at WSG, allows an opportunity to explore another culture in depth, studying the similarities and differences between our own British values and lifestyle with that of another country.
The teaching in KS2 (supported by the Rising Stars Scheme) helps teach this awareness to the children in appropriate, relevant topics that interest them – such as school, weather and food.
Opportunities for incidental learning of languages surround the children – for example, children learn about other languages and cultures in whole school assemblies and year group based topics.
We value the importance of our children seeing themselves as global citizens and understanding that they have a place in a wide range of communities extending beyond the WSG gates. The value we place on this is at the heart of MFL teaching at WSG.

pageCache.pageTitle: Personal Development — Wonersh and Shamley Green
pageCache.text:
Personal Development
Nurturing Growth, Confidence, and Well-being
At Wonersh and Shamley Green, we believe that personal development is just as important as academic achievement. Our Christian ethos guides us in creating a supportive and inclusive environment where every child can flourish as an individual.
Our Approach to Personal Development
We focus on helping children develop:
Resilience and Growth Mindset: We encourage children to embrace challenges, learn from mistakes, and celebrate their progress.
Self-Awareness and Emotional Intelligence: Children learn to understand their emotions, build healthy relationships, and develop empathy for others.
Responsibility and Leadership: Through classroom roles, school projects, and community initiatives, we empower children to take ownership and make positive contributions.
Kindness and Respect: Our core values of kindness, respect, and tolerance create a sense of belonging where everyone feels valued.
Spiritual Development: We offer opportunities for reflection, exploring big questions, and celebrating the wonder of the world around them.
How We Embed Personal Development
PSHE Curriculum (Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education): Dedicated lessons provide space to explore topics like self-esteem, healthy relationships, and making responsible choices.
Assemblies and Collective Worship: We share stories, values, and celebrate acts of kindness that inspire personal growth.
Outdoor Learning & Forest School: Experiences in nature foster resilience, problem-solving skills, and a sense of connection.
Clubs and Activities: Opportunities for leadership, teamwork, and exploring personal interests.
Partnership with Families: We encourage open communication with parents to support children's development both at school and at home.
The Whole Child Matters
Our goal is to nurture confident, compassionate, and well-rounded individuals who are ready to make a positive impact on their communities and the world.

Music
Music plays an integral part in the life of our school. We see it as an important aspect of our creative curriculum.
The staff and children organise and design the church services we perform to the school and local communities of Shamley Green and Wonersh. These include the Harvest Festival and Easter Service and Shamley Green Church, and the Christmas Service at Wonersh Church. We also sing at the carol service for older people in Wonersh. Year 6 and Year 2 lead a remembrance service at Wonersh Church.
We regularly sing as a whole school recognising the benefits of singing and music; improved self-confidence, physical and emotional health; learning to work collaboratively as part of small and large teams; and having the confidence to perform in front of peers and the wider community.
We have a range of clubs and classes on offer to all children run by external professionals and in conjunction with Surrey Arts, Boogie Pumps and Open to Music. These include piano lessons; guitar lessons; ensemble groups; choir; dance classes; drama workshops; and art clubs. These clubs give children opportunities to succeed, to learn new skills and create behaviours for learning which are embedded throughout the school.
We recognise the emotional needs of children who are well supported through our commitment to the Arts. We provide high-quality experiences both in and out of school and respond flexibly to needs and opportunities as they arise We work closely with professional arts practitioners. Delivering the curriculum in this way has created lifelong, memorable and inspiring experiences that improve the attainment and behaviour of all children.
These opportunities promote equality as we ensure that all children have access to each opportunity whatever their background. Some recent examples of these experiences include; singing in an opera at the Royal Albert Hall; participating in the Young Voices concert at the 02 Arena; taking part in Prom Praise at the Royal Albert Hall, Taking part in the Dorking Halls Music Festival, learning the ukulele and drumming workshops.

Physical Education & Sport
Sport Godalming Annual Awards 2025
Junior School of the Year
We are very proud of being recognised with this accolade and have new trophies to add to our ever-growing cabinet.
We aim to instill a love of sport and exercise in the children at WSG. This is vital for both physical and mental wellbeing and can be such a source of fun. We teach vital teamwork skills, which are transferable into many different areas of life. We aim to have fit, healthy children with an awareness of a healthy lifestyle. An understanding of the importance of this is proven to improve happiness, alertness and performance.
We aim for our children to experience competitive sport and be successful in these competitions, through good preparation and teaching. We enter a large number of tournaments, including some targeting SEND children in order to give every child the chance to compete and represent the school. When at events, we aim to instill good sportsmanship and teamwork skills that will stay with the children throughout their lives

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading and Phonics — Wonersh and Shamley Green
pageCache.text:
Reading and phonics
Videos for parents to explain how we teach phonics and Early Reading at WSG
Phonics is a way of teaching children how to read and write. It helps children hear, identify and use different sounds that distinguish one word from another in the English language.Written language can be compared to a code, so knowing the sounds of individual letters and how those letters sound when they’re combined will help children decode words as they read.
Understanding phonics will also help children know which letters to use when they are writing words.
The school uses the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds programme to teach phonics. Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised is a complete systematic synthetic phonics programme (SSP) developed for schools by schools. It meets all the expectations of the National Curriculum and prepares our children to go beyond the expectations of the Phonics Screening Check.
Supporting Reading at Home
We encourage our children to read as much as possible and you can support your child to develop a love of reading in many different ways. This helpful guide produced by the Education Endowment Fund gives 7 top tips to support reading at home.
EEF 7 Top Tips to Support Reading at Home
Learning to read is crucial to a child's development and for their access to the curriculum. The WSG Reading House represents a visual summary of the component parts of reading. This supports us to teach the different aspects of reading and diagnose what individual children need to work on to become fluent readers with excellent understanding. Our Reading House has been adapted from the one produced by the Education Endowment Foundation.
Look at our Reading House in detail here

Special educational needs and disability
At Wonersh and Shamley Green Church of England Primary School, we are committed to offering an inclusive curriculum to ensure the best possible progress for all of our pupils whatever their needs or abilities.
Central to our SEND work is the core belief that every teacher is a teacher of every pupil, including those with special educational needs.
At Wonersh and Shamley Green Primary School we want each child to achieve his/her best, to become confident individuals living fulfilling lives and to make a successful transition into their next school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Academic Development — Wonersh and Shamley Green
pageCache.text:
Academic Development
Nurturing a Love of Learning, Inspiring Excellence
At Wonersh and Shamley Green, we believe every child holds the potential to become a confident, enthusiastic, and successful learner. Our approach to academic development is grounded in our Christian values, fostering a safe and supportive environment where children can explore, take risks, and grow.
Our Curriculum: A learning adventure with kindness
We deliver a broad, stimulating, and engaging curriculum designed to:
Ignite Curiosity: Hands-on experiences, exciting projects, and exploration of our beautiful surroundings spark a natural love of learning.
Develop Essential Skills: We provide a strong foundation in literacy, numeracy, and critical thinking skills, essential for lifelong success.
Celebrate Creativity: Art, music, drama, and technology are woven into our curriculum, encouraging self-expression and innovative problem-solving.
Reflect and Grow: Learning how to learn is key. We help children reflect on their progress, embrace challenges, and learn from their experiences.
Beyond the Classroom: Enrichment for All
Forest School: Our woodlands offer unique opportunities for hands-on learning, connecting children with nature and building resilience.
Global Connections: Partnerships with international schools broaden our children's perspectives and help them understand their role as global citizens.
Trips and Experiences: Field trips, visiting speakers, and workshops bring learning to life, expanding horizons and igniting passions.
Supporting Every Child's Journey
Differentiated Learning: We recognise that every child learns differently and tailor our teaching to individual needs and strengths.
Nurturing Environment: Our Christian ethos fosters kindness, respect, and a sense of belonging, creating a space where everyone feels encouraged to reach their full potential.
Partnership with Parents: We believe parents are partners in their child's education and maintain open communication to support learning at home.
Our Commitment to Excellence
We are dedicated to providing exceptional academic opportunities for all our students. Our dedicated teachers receive ongoing professional development to ensure they deliver the highest quality learning experiences.

Computing
The aims of our computing curriculum are:
To empower pupils with the skills and knowledge to navigate and use the internet wisely and safely.
To give each pupil the opportunity to develop and apply computational thinking skills across a wide range of situations and tasks.
To develop computational thinkers who show resilience when carrying out problem solving tasks.
To enhance teamwork and communication skills.
To allow children to become confident with a range of digital devices so they can apply effective ICT skills in their learning across the curriculum.
To ensure pupils become digitally savvy so they are active participants in a digital world and are able to develop their ideas using information and communication technology skills at a level suitable for the future workplace.
